 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The  Philadelphia 76ers  are known for having one of the most passionate, knowledgeable, and unforgiving fan bases in the NBA. Home to all-time greats like Wilt Chamberlain, Julius Erving, Moses Malone, Charles Barkley and Allen Iverson, wearing a Sixers jersey brings a sense of responsibility, especially to the people of Philly. 
 However, some players have learned this the hard way, Ben Simmons being one of the most recent examples. Whether you're a well-established name or in the initial years of your career, nobody is safe from fan scrutiny in Philly, which is why former Sixers forward  Georges Niang  wanted to go into hiding on one such occasion.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Poor sequence
 The  situation  involved Niang missing a game-tying 3-pointer that struck the backboard. Immediately securing the rebound, he missed a subsequent one-handed floater as well. More concerning, though, was his decision-making in attempting a two-point shot with less than 3.5 seconds remaining in regulation, with the 76ers being down by three. 
 Adding to it,  James Harden  and Tyrese Maxey stood relatively open at the 3-point line. The game in question took place between the 76ers and Denver Nuggets during the 2021-22 season. Revisiting the embarrassing moment recently on the "Not Even D2" podcast, Niang shared how Harden became his savior. 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Beard helped him regain his confidence
 After his late-game blunder against the Nuggets, Niang wanted to stay under the radar for a while. During this time, he found a great source of strength in Harden, who reassured him after Harden let him into the back room of the lounge he'd booked for dinner. 
 "I don't really want to be out in public cause, you know, in Philly, like I just blew the game. So, I called him (Harden), and I was like, surprised he actually picked up.  ' Like, can I just hop in the back room with you?'  Niang  asked  the 2018 NBA MVP, who was gracious enough.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Yeah, absolutely, bro. Like, you know, 100 percent. Don't sweat what happened. We got another one on Thursday,"  said Niang, quoting what Harden told him. 
 Lamenting blowing the game against the Nuggets, Georges never expected such kind of assurance from James, who, meanwhile, had just joined the 76ers midway through the 2021-22 season. 
 "Like, let's enjoy dinner and have a good time and get the next game,"  Harden told Niang, who always felt The Beard  deserved more respect  than he received.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Related: "He's been pretty much a jerk almost his entire life" – Nuggets coach slammed Kareem Abdul-Jabbar before his final All-Star Game 
 Learning from the veteran scorer 
 Teammates for close to a season and a half, Niang took a lot away from his partnership with Harden. Beyond the scoring, Georges was most impressed by James' playmaking and how he read the game, whether setting timely screens or finding his teammates in the right spot.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I was sometimes almost like, 'This might be the best part of his game,' because I would just move to a certain direction, catch the ball, and the only thing I had to do was shoot," said  the 33-year-old, describing how Harden was one of the most unselfish players and always took care of the young guys on the roster.
 As his game shows in recent years, Harden has clearly transitioned into more of a facilitator. The three-time scoring champion has clearly taken on the role of a veteran leader and does not mind being the second option on a team while helping others.
